skin.note: Three-colour palette from a halved Hass avocado: Skin #3b4320 (light accent, footer band; 10.34:1 on paper), Flesh #d8de8a (dark accent, fills; 13.54:1 on #0f0e0c), Pit #7a4a2b (small marks only). Text on Flesh is #23280f.

signal-violet.note: Narrow brief: second stop of the gradient micro-label and the ambient scan-line. Never a state, never a category.

accent-shared.note: The unscoped :root accent. gradeVITian runs on it; the portfolio overrides it. Not the portfolio's colour.

bg.note: Normative intent is cool blue-slate newsprint; the shipped hex carries a warm cast. Known drift, correction pending (The Cool Newsprint Rule).

border.note: The standard hairline. Divides ruled bands and outlines tiles.

border-strong.note: Where a rule begins and where a pull-quote hangs.

fg.note: Top of the four-step ink ramp. Full ink is the system's emphasis device (The One Ink Rule).

fg-faint.note: Dormant state. Anything not live and not distinguished sits here.

display.purpose: Hero headline only. EB Garamond via .display-serif + .display-xl. Modest vw factor so the headline never pushes the CTAs and signature below the fold.

headline.purpose: Chapter labels in the home page rail (.display-md).

title.purpose: Card and section headings. Instrument Sans 600.

body.purpose: All UI and card copy at 15px/1.55.

prose.purpose: /blog and /lab article bodies. Source Serif 4, 68ch, Garamond headings, indigo drop cap. Never themed away.

voice-serif.purpose: Pull-quotes, opinions, origin story. Garamond at reading size with text-wrap: pretty.

dateline.purpose: PLACE / YEAR above a filed chapter, and every measurement line beneath one. Geist Mono, tabular.

label.purpose: Section micro-labels and stat captions. 10px, uppercase, 0.2em.

signature.purpose: The fine-nib italic mark standing in for a handwritten signature. One consumer.

marginalia.purpose: The hero doodle field only. Caveat, variable weight axis, one consumer.

shadows.name: card-rest-light
shadows.purpose: The default in light mode. Hairline borders and the two paper tints carry depth; there is no resting shadow.

shadows.name: card-rest-dark
shadows.purpose: The minimum needed to hold a card edge against true black.

shadows.name: card-hover-light
shadows.purpose: Applied by .card-lift on hover of an interactive tile, paired with translateY(-3px).

shadows.name: card-hover-dark
shadows.purpose: The same gesture on black; more layers to stay readable.

shadows.name: stack
shadows.purpose: Upward cast under a stacked section (.stack-sect). 0.50 alpha in dark.

shadows.name: reading-spotlight
shadows.purpose: Reading mode dims the page with a giant shadow rather than an overlay, so it survives ancestor stacking contexts.

shadows.name: focus-ring-chat
shadows.purpose: The chat input's focus state — a page-coloured gap then an indigo ring, instead of a border shift.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The site's primary curve. Scroll reveals (550ms), card lift (300ms), bubble-in, drawer. Fast out, long settle.

motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: The pen curve. Page transition (400ms), the ink rule drawing itself left-to-right (900ms), the doodle ink stroke (820ms), the hang-tag swing.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Global button press. Cards settle to scale(0.99) on the same duration.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: The only resting-to-raised transition in the system.

motion.name: sweep
motion.purpose: The accent hairline wiping across a tile's top edge on hover.

motion.name: theme-swap
motion.value: background-color 0.25s ease, color 0.25s ease, border-color 0.25s ease, box-shadow 0.25s ease
motion.purpose: Body-level transition so a theme change reads as a dissolve.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Kills scroll-behavior, every ambient loop, .animate-ping, .animate-pulse, and all entrance animations — and resets the property each one holds hostage (scaleX(1), stroke-dashoffset: 0, opacity: 0) rather than only stopping the animation.

narrative.overview:
The site is a printed thing that happens to run in a browser. Its material is newsprint and ink: an off-white sheet, a deep near-black ink, hairline column rules doing the work that boxes and shadows do elsewhere. Nothing floats decoratively; where something lifts, it lifts because you touched it.

The organizing idea is that type is casting, not decoration. Instrument Sans is the system talking — chrome, labels, UI copy, bound under `html:has(.portfolio)` so it covers every portfolio route and /chat while gradeVITian and VRF Bricks keep their own faces. EB Garamond (and Cormorant for the signature) is the author talking — hero and chapter headlines, pull-quotes, opinions, the signature mark. Geist Mono is the machine reporting — measurements, datelines, uptime counters, model ids, anything the build knows rather than claims. Source Serif 4 is the reader's voice — long-form /blog and /lab prose, set at reading size and never themed away. A visitor should be able to tell who is speaking without reading a word.

Density is editorial, not dashboard: one column, generous vertical rhythm between chapters, tight leading inside them. Colour is almost entirely absent — the page is ink on paper, and a single indigo appears only where something is alive. The confirmed anti-reference is the generic developer-portfolio dark mode: neon-on-charcoal, gradient hero, glassmorphic cards, a rainbow of tag colours. This system rejects all of it.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-on-paper primaries; a cool newsprint sheet and a deep near-black ink
One accent, Signal Indigo, reserved for live state
Four assigned typefaces, each with a fixed speaker
Hairline rules and ruled bands instead of nested cards
Flat at rest; depth is earned by interaction
One continuous reading column at every viewport
Paper grain over the whole page (2.8% multiply noise, 1.8% screen in dark)

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is ink weight, not hue. A thing is important because it is set in full `fg` while its neighbours sit at `fg-subtle`, never because it was tinted. Audit test: desaturate a screen; if the hierarchy survives, it obeyed the rule.

rules.name: The Two Papers Rule
rules.body: There are two papers, `bg` and `surface`, plus a raised and a sunken step for edges. A surface never invents a third tint, a tinted card, or a coloured panel.

rules.name: The Cool Newsprint Rule
rules.body: The neutral ramp is normatively cool blue-slate — quality newsprint under natural light. The shipped hexes carry a warm cast (#fefefb / #181410) that is known drift, not intent; the correction is still pending. New neutrals are chosen cool.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Indigo means live: something running, open, active, or focused. It is not a brand wash, not a category colour, and not a hover flourish on a static element. Live is indigo, distinguished is full ink, dormant is faint — three states, one hue.

rules.name: The No-Category-Colour Rule
rules.body: Tags, skills, project types, roles and post kinds are never colour-coded. They are distinguished by ink weight, rule weight, and position.

rules.name: The Assigned Speaker Rule
rules.body: Four faces, four speakers: Instrument Sans is the system, Garamond/Cormorant is the author, Geist Mono is the machine, Source Serif 4 is the reader. Before setting a new string, name its speaker; that names the face. A measurement never appears in Garamond, and an opinion never appears in mono.

rules.name: The Unthemeable Voice Rule
rules.body: `--font-garamond`, `--font-cormorant` and `--font-blog` are deliberately never overridden by `[data-theme]`. The author's voice and the reader's voice survive every theme; only the system's voice swaps.

rules.name: The Escape Hatch Rule
rules.body: `--font-display` is overridden in exactly one place: `html:has(.portfolio)` points it at Garamond, making Garamond the portfolio's one display voice (h1 and the hero name band included). Never override it per theme or at `:root`; gradeVITian and VRF Bricks inherit the root value and must stay grotesque. Inside components, keep reaching for `.display-serif`.

rules.name: The Ghost Numeral Rule
rules.body: A chapter is counted once, by the oversized ghost numeral in the rail. No second mono numeral, no third line above the heading; the dateline below carries the filing.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: The page is one column of reading at every width. Side rails carry identity, never content the reader must have. A layout that only works above `lg` is not a layout.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Every run of text declares its measure. Nothing sets wider than 72ch, and prose sets at 68ch.

rules.name: The Earned Depth Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat until touched. Shadow is the response to hover, focus, or press — never a resting decoration, and never a substitute for a rule or a tint.

rules.name: The Ruled Band Rule
rules.body: A group of related figures is a ruled band — `border-y` on the group, `divide-x` between the cells — not a row of cards. Cards nested inside cards are the failure mode this replaced; every line in a band is present at rest, never gated behind a hover a touch device cannot reach.

rules.name: The No-Scrim Rule
rules.body: The nav meets content at a clean edge. It carries the page background, not a translucent wash — a scrim over the sticky chrome dropped body copy behind it to roughly 2:1 and was removed.

rules.name: The Three Corners Rule
rules.body: Chip, panel, card. A new surface picks one of the three or it picks the pill because it is an action. There is no fourth radius.

rules.name: The Rule Before The Box Rule
rules.body: Reach for a hairline before a container. If a border, a gradient rule, or a divided band can express the grouping, it does — a bordered box is the last resort, not the first.

rules.name: The Two Curves Rule
rules.body: The system has two easing curves and no third: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for a surface settling into place, and cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) for a stroke being drawn. Every transition picks one.

dos: Do name the speaker before choosing a face: system (Instrument Sans), author (Garamond/Cormorant), machine (Geist Mono), reader (Source Serif 4).
Do build hierarchy from the four-step ink ramp — fg → fg-muted → fg-subtle → fg-faint — before reaching for any colour.
Do reserve Signal Indigo for live state: running, open, active, focused.
Do express a group of figures as a ruled band (border-y + divide-x) at reading scale, with every line visible at rest.
Do pick one of the three corners (chip 0.5rem, panel 0.75rem, card 1rem), or the pill if it is an action.
Do cap the measure — 68ch for prose, 72ch for bullet lists, 62ch for body columns.
Do let depth be earned: flat at rest, card-lift on hover, 0.97 on press.
Do file a real deployment with a mono PLACE / YEAR dateline and a mono measure line.

Do add every new ambient or infinite animation to the prefers-reduced-motion block, and reset the property it holds hostage (scaleX(1), stroke-dashoffset: 0, opacity: 0) rather than only killing the animation.
Do keep the author's and reader's faces out of --font-display; that variable is the theme escape hatch.
donts: Don't colour-code categories, tags, skills, or post types. No emerald/teal/amber/orange/sky/violet ramps on reading surfaces.
Don't introduce a third paper tint or a tinted card to signal state; invert to ink instead.
Don't nest a card inside a card. If it needs grouping, rule it.
Don't put a scrim, wash, or blur behind the sticky nav over body content.
Don't gate information behind hover — a touch device will never see it.
Don't add a resting shadow in light mode; --shadow-card is none there on purpose.
Don't invent a fourth radius or a bespoke per-component corner.
Don't set a measurement in a serif or an opinion in mono.
Don't reach for the generic developer-portfolio dark mode: neon on charcoal, gradient heroes, glass cards, rainbow tags.
